questions.q: Which state of matter has a definite volume but no definite shape?
questions.explanation: A liquid keeps its volume but takes the shape of its container.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of temperature?
questions.explanation: The SI unit of temperature is the kelvin (K).

questions.q: The change of a solid directly into a gas without passing through the liquid state is called
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the direct change of a solid into vapour, as seen with camphor or naphthalene.

questions.q: Water freezes at 0 °C. On the kelvin scale, rounded to a whole number, this temperature is
Gases can be compressed easily because
options: their particles have very large spaces between them
questions.explanation: Large inter-particle spaces in a gas allow the particles to be pushed closer together.

questions.q: Wet clothes dry faster on a windy day than on a still day because the wind
options: makes the water in the clothes boil
carries away water vapour, which speeds up evaporation
freezes the water on the clothes
increases the humidity of the air near the clothes
questions.explanation: Moving air removes water vapour near the cloth, so more water evaporates in the same time.

questions.q: While ice is melting in a beaker over a flame, the thermometer keeps reading 0 °C even though heat is supplied. This is because
options: all the heat is lost to the surroundings
the heat supplied is used to overcome the forces between particles (latent heat of fusion)
ice does not absorb heat while melting
questions.explanation: The heat of fusion breaks the particle arrangement of the solid, so the temperature does not rise until all the ice has melted.

questions.q: What is evaporation? Name two factors that increase its rate.
questions.answer: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour at any temperature below its boiling point, taking place at the surface. Its rate increases with a larger surface area and with a higher temperature (also with less humidity and more wind).
keyPoints: Liquid changes to vapour below boiling point
Rate rises with temperature, wind or lower humidity
questions.explanation: Faster-moving surface particles escape into the air, so conditions that help them escape raise the rate.

questions.q: Why do we feel cooler after sweating when we sit under a fan?
questions.answer: Sweat on the skin evaporates. The particles of water need energy to change into vapour and take this latent heat from the body, which cools us. The fan blows away the vapour and makes evaporation faster.
keyPoints: Evaporation takes heat from the body
questions.explanation: Evaporation is a cooling process because the escaping particles absorb heat from the surface.

questions.q: Which of the following is a pure substance?
questions.explanation: Distilled water contains only water, a compound, so it is a pure substance.

questions.q: Which of the following is a mixture?
questions.explanation: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc, so it is a homogeneous mixture.

questions.q: Common salt is obtained from sea water by
questions.explanation: On heating sea water the water evaporates and the salt is left behind.

questions.q: Which method separates a mixture of common salt and ammonium chloride?
questions.explanation: Ammonium chloride sublimes on heating while common salt does not.

questions.q: Which of the following shows the Tyndall effect?
questions.explanation: Milk is a colloid whose particles are large enough to scatter a beam of light.

questions.q: A separating funnel can be used to separate oil from water because the two liquids
options: are immiscible and form separate layers
questions.explanation: Immiscible liquids form two layers, and the lower one can be run off through the tap.

questions.q: A beam of light is clearly visible when passed through a liquid. The particles do not settle on standing and cannot be removed by ordinary filtration. The liquid is a
questions.explanation: A colloid scatters light but its particles stay dispersed and pass through filter paper; a suspension would settle.

questions.q: Give two differences between a compound and a mixture.
questions.answer: A compound is formed by chemical combination of elements in a fixed ratio by mass and has properties different from its elements. A mixture can have any proportion of its components, which keep their own properties and can be separated by physical methods.
keyPoints: Compound has fixed composition, mixture variable
questions.explanation: Compounds involve chemical bonding; mixtures are only physically combined.

questions.q: How would you separate a mixture of sand, common salt and iron filings?
questions.answer: First pass a magnet over the mixture to remove the iron filings. Add water to the remaining mixture to dissolve the salt and filter it, so the sand stays on the filter paper. Evaporate the filtrate to get the salt.
questions.explanation: Each step uses a different property: magnetism, solubility and volatility of the solvent.

questions.q: The law of conservation of mass was put forward by
questions.explanation: Lavoisier showed that mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.

questions.q: The chemical symbol of sodium is
questions.explanation: The symbol Na comes from the Latin name natrium.

questions.q: What is the chemical formula of water?
questions.explanation: A water molecule has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

questions.q: How many atoms are present in one molecule of sulphuric acid, H2SO4?
questions.explanation: 2 hydrogen + 1 sulphur + 4 oxygen = 7 atoms.

questions.q: The molecular mass of carbon dioxide, CO2, is (C = 12 u, O = 16 u)
How many moles are present in 11 g of carbon dioxide (molar mass 44 g/mol)?
questions.explanation: Moles = mass / molar mass = 11 / 44 = 0.25.

questions.q: Samples of pure water from a river and from rain are both found to contain hydrogen and oxygen in the mass ratio 1 : 8. Which law does this illustrate?
questions.explanation: A pure compound always has its elements in a fixed ratio by mass, whatever its source.

questions.q: State the law of conservation of mass and give an example.
questions.answer: In a chemical reaction the total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products; mass is neither created nor destroyed. For example, when 12 g of carbon burns in 32 g of oxygen, 44 g of carbon dioxide is formed.
keyPoints: Mass is neither created nor destroyed
Total mass of reactants equals products
questions.explanation: Atoms are only rearranged in a reaction, so total mass stays the same.

questions.q: Calculate the number of molecules in 0.5 mole of a gas. (Avogadro constant = 6.022 × 10^23 per mole)
questions.answer: Number of molecules = moles × Avogadro constant = 0.5 × 6.022 × 10^23 = 3.011 × 10^23 molecules.
questions.explanation: One mole contains 6.022 × 10^23 particles, so half a mole contains half that number.

questions.q: Who discovered the atomic nucleus through the gold foil experiment?
questions.explanation: Rutherford's alpha-particle scattering experiment led to the nuclear model of the atom.

questions.q: Which subatomic particle carries no electric charge?
questions.explanation: The neutron is electrically neutral.

questions.q: The electron was discovered by
questions.explanation: J.J. Thomson discovered the electron and proposed the plum-pudding model.

questions.q: The atomic number of an element is equal to the number of
questions.explanation: Atomic number Z is the number of protons in the nucleus.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of electrons that the M shell (third shell) can hold?
questions.explanation: The 2n² rule gives 2 × 3² = 18 electrons.

questions.q: An atom has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 1. Its valency is
questions.explanation: The atom has one electron in its outermost shell and can lose it, so its valency is 1.

questions.q: Two atoms both have mass number 40, but their atomic numbers are 18 and 20. They are called
questions.explanation: Atoms of different elements with the same mass number are isobars.

questions.q: State two drawbacks of Rutherford's model of the atom.
questions.answer: According to the model, electrons revolving around the nucleus would be accelerating and lose energy, so they should spiral into the nucleus and the atom would collapse. The model also could not explain why atoms are stable.
questions.explanation: Bohr's model overcame this with fixed energy levels (shells).

questions.q: Chlorine occurs as two isotopes, Cl-35 and Cl-37, yet its atomic mass is given as 35.5 u. Explain.
questions.answer: The atomic mass of an element is the average of the masses of its isotopes weighted by their natural abundance. Cl-35 is more abundant (about three times Cl-37), so the average is 35.5 u, not a whole number.
questions.explanation: No single chlorine atom has mass 35.5 u; this is an average over the natural mixture.

questions.q: Who first observed cells in a thin slice of cork?
questions.explanation: Robert Hooke saw the box-like cells of cork under a microscope in 1665.

questions.q: Which cell organelle is called the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria release the energy of food as ATP.

questions.q: The cell wall of a plant cell is mainly made of
questions.explanation: Plant cell walls are made chiefly of cellulose.

questions.q: Who discovered the nucleus in the cell?
questions.explanation: Robert Brown described the nucleus in 1831.

questions.q: Osmosis is the movement of
options: water across a selectively permeable membrane from a region of higher water concentration to lower water concentration
solute particles from low to high concentration using energy
gases from a region of high to low pressure
solid particles through the cell wall
questions.explanation: Osmosis is the diffusion of water through a selectively permeable membrane.

questions.q: Which organelles are known as the suicide bags of the cell?
questions.explanation: If a cell is damaged, lysosomes burst and their enzymes digest the cell.

questions.q: Red blood cells are placed in a very concentrated salt solution. They shrink because
options: water enters the cells by osmosis
water leaves the cells by osmosis
questions.explanation: The surrounding solution is more concentrated, so water moves out of the cells.

questions.q: State two differences between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
questions.answer: A prokaryotic cell has no well-defined nucleus (no nuclear membrane) and no membrane-bound organelles, while a eukaryotic cell has a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles. Prokaryotic cells are generally smaller, for example bacteria.
questions.explanation: The key difference is the presence or absence of a membrane-bound nucleus.

questions.q: Potato cubes are placed in distilled water and in a concentrated sugar solution. Predict what happens to each and explain.
questions.answer: In distilled water the potato cubes gain water by osmosis and become firm and larger. In concentrated sugar solution they lose water by osmosis and shrink, because water moves toward the region with the lower water concentration.
keyPoints: Distilled water: water enters, cube swells
Sugar solution: water leaves, cube shrinks
Water moves by osmosis across the membrane
questions.explanation: Direction of water movement depends on the relative concentration inside and outside the cells.

questions.q: Which tissue carries water and minerals upward in a plant?
questions.explanation: Xylem conducts water and minerals from the roots to the leaves.

questions.q: Which structure connects muscle to bone?
questions.explanation: Tendons are strong fibrous tissues that join muscle to bone.

questions.q: The structural and functional unit of nervous tissue is the
questions.explanation: A neuron is a nerve cell that carries impulses.

questions.q: Which meristem is responsible for the increase in the girth (thickness) of a stem?
questions.explanation: Lateral meristem (cambium) adds to the thickness of stems and roots.

questions.q: Which of these muscles works under the control of our will?
options: The muscle of the heart wall
The muscle in the wall of the intestine
The muscle that controls the pupil of the eye
The biceps muscle of the arm
questions.explanation: The biceps is a skeletal muscle, which is voluntary.

questions.q: A leaf that has lost much water droops, and the guard cells of its stomata change shape. The guard cells mainly control
options: the opening and closing of the stomata
the transport of food to the roots
the thickness of the cell wall
the growth in length of the leaf
questions.explanation: Guard cells open and close the stomatal pore, controlling gas exchange and water loss.

questions.q: Leaf stalks and tender stems bend in the wind without breaking. Which tissue gives them this flexibility?
questions.explanation: Collenchyma has thickened corners that give flexibility with mechanical support.

questions.q: Write two differences between xylem and phloem.
questions.answer: Xylem transports water and minerals from roots to other parts, and most of its cells are dead. Phloem transports food (sugars) prepared in leaves to other parts, and its sieve tubes are living cells.
questions.explanation: Together they form the complex conducting tissues of plants.

questions.q: What would happen to a shoot if its apical meristem were removed? Give a reason.
questions.answer: The shoot would stop growing in length, because cell division at the tip, which adds new cells that elongate the stem, would no longer take place.
keyPoints: Apical meristem divides at the tip
Division adds cells that elongate stem
questions.explanation: Apical meristem is responsible for the increase in length of shoots and roots.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of velocity?
questions.explanation: Velocity is displacement per unit time, measured in metres per second.

questions.q: The slope of a distance-time graph gives
questions.explanation: Slope is change in distance divided by change in time, which is speed.

questions.q: Which of these quantities has both magnitude and direction?
questions.explanation: Velocity is a vector; the others are scalars.

questions.q: A car covers 60 km in 1.5 hours. Its average speed is
questions.explanation: Speed = 60 km / 1.5 h = 40 km/h.

questions.q: A body starts from rest and has a uniform acceleration of 2 m/s². Its velocity after 5 s is
An athlete completes exactly one full round of a circular track of radius r. Her displacement is
questions.explanation: She ends at the starting point, so the displacement is zero although the distance is 2πr.

questions.q: A car moving at 20 m/s is brought to rest in 5 s by uniform braking. Taking the direction of motion as positive, its acceleration is
questions.explanation: a = (0 − 20) / 5 = −4 m/s²; the negative sign shows retardation.

questions.q: Differentiate between distance and displacement.
questions.answer: Distance is the total length of the path travelled and is a scalar that is never negative. Displacement is the shortest straight-line distance from the initial to the final position with a direction, and it is a vector that can be zero.
keyPoints: Displacement is shortest change in position, vector
Displacement can be zero or negative
questions.explanation: Displacement depends only on end points, distance depends on the path.

questions.q: A bus increases its speed from 10 m/s to 30 m/s in 10 s. Find its acceleration and the distance it covers in this time.
questions.answer: Acceleration a = (30 − 10) / 10 = 2 m/s². Distance s = (v² − u²) / 2a = (900 − 100) / 4 = 200 m.
questions.explanation: Both answers use the equations of uniformly accelerated motion; average speed 20 m/s × 10 s also gives 200 m.

questions.q: The law of inertia is which of Newton's laws of motion?
questions.explanation: Newton's first law says a body stays at rest or in uniform motion unless acted on by an unbalanced force.

questions.q: The SI unit of force is the
questions.explanation: One newton is the force that gives a 1 kg mass an acceleration of 1 m/s².

questions.q: The momentum of a body is defined as
questions.explanation: Momentum p = m × v.

questions.q: What force is needed to give a 5 kg body an acceleration of 3 m/s²?
A rocket moves forward by throwing hot gases backward. This is an example of
options: the law of conservation of energy
questions.explanation: The gases are pushed back and an equal and opposite force pushes the rocket forward.

questions.q: Passengers in a bus are thrown forward when the driver brakes suddenly. The reason is that
options: the bus pushes the passengers forward
the passengers' bodies tend to continue in their state of motion
questions.explanation: Inertia keeps the upper body moving forward while the bus slows down.

questions.q: A 4 kg gun fires a 0.02 kg bullet at 100 m/s. The recoil speed of the gun is
questions.explanation: By conservation of momentum, 4 × v = 0.02 × 100, so v = 0.5 m/s.

questions.q: State Newton's second law of motion and write its mathematical form.
questions.answer: The rate of change of momentum of a body is directly proportional to the applied unbalanced force and takes place in the direction of the force. For constant mass, F = ma.
keyPoints: Rate of change of momentum proportional to force
questions.explanation: The law gives the way to measure force from mass and acceleration.

questions.q: Why does a cricketer pull his hands backward while catching a fast cricket ball?
questions.answer: By moving the hands back, the cricketer increases the time over which the ball's momentum is brought to zero. A longer time means a smaller rate of change of momentum, so the force on the hands is smaller and they are not hurt.
keyPoints: Rate of change of momentum decreases
questions.explanation: F = change in momentum / time, so a larger time reduces the force.

questions.q: The acceleration due to gravity near the Earth's surface is about
questions.explanation: g is approximately 9.8 m/s² on Earth.

questions.q: Weight of an object is measured in
questions.explanation: Weight is the force of gravity on a body, so its unit is the newton.

questions.q: What is the weight of a 10 kg object on Earth? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
The acceleration due to gravity on the Moon is about one-sixth of that on Earth. A person of mass 60 kg on the Moon has a mass of
questions.explanation: Mass does not depend on location; only the weight changes.

questions.q: A heavy stone and a light feather are dropped together from the same height in a vacuum. They
options: reach the ground at the same time
questions.explanation: With no air resistance every body falls with the same acceleration g.

questions.q: If the distance between two masses is doubled, the gravitational force between them becomes
questions.explanation: Force varies inversely as the square of the distance, so doubling d divides F by 4.

questions.q: State the universal law of gravitation.
questions.answer: Every object in the universe attracts every other object with a force that is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them, F = G m1 m2 / r².
keyPoints: Inversely proportional to square of distance
questions.explanation: The force acts along the line joining the centres of the two objects.

questions.q: Why is the value of g slightly greater at the poles than at the equator?
questions.answer: The Earth is not a perfect sphere; it is slightly flattened at the poles, so the poles are nearer to the centre of the Earth. Since g is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the centre, g is larger at the poles.
keyPoints: Poles are closer to the centre
g varies inversely with square of radius
questions.explanation: A smaller radius at the poles gives a greater value of g.

questions.q: The SI unit of work is the
questions.explanation: Work is measured in joules; one joule is one newton-metre.

questions.q: The energy possessed by a body due to its motion is called
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is the energy of motion, KE = ½mv².

questions.q: What is the potential energy of a 2 kg object at a height of 5 m? (take g = 10 m/s²)
The kinetic energy of a 2 kg object moving at 3 m/s is
A girl carries a bag and walks along a level road. The work done by the upward force she applies on the bag is
questions.explanation: The force is vertical while the displacement is horizontal, so no work is done by it.

questions.q: A 60 W bulb is switched on for 5 hours. The electrical energy it uses is
questions.explanation: Energy = 0.06 kW × 5 h = 0.3 kWh.

questions.q: State the law of conservation of energy.
questions.answer: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed; it can only be changed from one form into another. The total energy of an isolated system remains constant.
keyPoints: Energy is not created or destroyed
It changes from one form to another
questions.explanation: In every transformation the total amount of energy stays the same.

questions.q: Describe the energy changes in a swinging pendulum bob.
questions.answer: At the extreme positions the bob is momentarily at rest and has maximum potential energy. As it swings down, potential energy changes to kinetic energy, which is maximum at the lowest point. The total energy stays constant if air resistance is ignored.
questions.explanation: In reality a little energy is lost as heat, so the pendulum gradually stops.

questions.q: Sound cannot travel through
questions.explanation: Sound needs a material medium to travel.

questions.q: The SI unit of frequency is the
questions.explanation: One hertz is one oscillation per second.

questions.q: The audible range of frequency for normal human ears is about
questions.explanation: Humans generally hear sounds from 20 Hz to 20 kHz.

questions.q: Sound waves in air are
questions.explanation: Particles of air vibrate back and forth along the direction in which the wave travels.

questions.q: To hear a distinct echo, the reflecting surface must be at least about how far from the source of sound (in air, ordinary temperature)?
questions.explanation: The sound must return after at least 0.1 s; at about 344 m/s the surface must be roughly 17 m away.

questions.q: We hear thunder some seconds after seeing the lightning because
options: thunder is produced after the lightning
light travels much faster than sound
the sound is absorbed by clouds
questions.explanation: Light travels at about 3 × 10^8 m/s while sound travels at only about 340 m/s in air.

questions.q: Distinguish between loudness and pitch of a sound.
questions.answer: Loudness depends on the amplitude of the vibration; a larger amplitude gives a louder sound. Pitch depends on the frequency; a higher frequency gives a higher pitch (shriller sound).
questions.explanation: Amplitude and frequency are different features of a wave.

questions.q: A person fires a gun and hears its echo from a cliff after 2 s. If the speed of sound is 340 m/s, how far is the cliff?
questions.answer: The sound travels to the cliff and back, so total distance = 340 × 2 = 680 m. The cliff is half of this distance away, i.e. 340 m.
keyPoints: Path is to the cliff and back
questions.explanation: The echo covers twice the distance to the reflector.

questions.q: Which of the following is a kharif crop?
questions.explanation: Paddy is sown in the rainy season (June to July) and is a kharif crop.

questions.q: Which of the following is a rabi crop?
questions.explanation: Wheat is sown in winter and harvested in spring, so it is a rabi crop.

questions.q: The rearing of fish is called
questions.explanation: Pisciculture means fish farming.

questions.q: Apiculture is the rearing of
questions.explanation: Apiculture or bee-keeping is done to get honey and wax.

questions.q: Manure is
options: a chemical fertiliser made in factories
an organic substance made by the decomposition of animal waste and plant residues
a mineral mined from the ground
questions.explanation: Manure is organic and adds nutrients and humus to the soil.

questions.q: Why do farmers grow different crops, such as a legume after a cereal, on the same field in succession?
options: To increase the number of weeds
To help maintain soil fertility and reduce pests and diseases
questions.explanation: Crop rotation avoids exhausting the same nutrients and legumes add nitrogen.

questions.q: What are macronutrients? Name any three.
questions.answer: Macronutrients are the nutrients that plants need in large quantities. Examples are nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, calcium, magnesium and sulphur.
keyPoints: Needed by plants in large amounts
Three named examples such as N, P, K
questions.explanation: Plants get these six elements from the soil in large amounts.

questions.q: What is intercropping? Give one example and one advantage.
questions.answer: Intercropping is growing two or more crops simultaneously in the same field in a definite pattern of rows. An example is soyabean with maize. Its advantage is that it reduces the risk of crop failure and makes better use of resources.
keyPoints: Two or more crops in definite row pattern
Example such as soyabean with maize
Better use of resources or less pest spread
questions.explanation: The crops chosen need different nutrients so they do not compete much.
